Today, Amazon-owned subsidiary Ring announced its first smart door lock, addressing a key issue that has plagued many smart lock users: dead batteries. Ring has come up with an ingenious solution to this problem, and the lock will go on sale in the first quarter of 2027. In addition, the company also unveiled several new security cameras with improved low-light performance.

Ring Smart Door Lock

The concept of a smart door lock isn't exactly new, but what Ring aims to solve is the dead battery issue of smart locks. To prevent you from being locked out at an inconvenient time, the Ring Smart Door Lock allows you to turn a manual dial several times to generate enough power to briefly operate the lock, letting you open the door and get inside right away.

The Ring Smart Door Lock has everything you'd expect from a smart lock: fingerprint unlock, a touch-sensitive numeric keypad, or the ability to open the door via your phone using the Ring app.

The Ring app also offers a range of features, including remote viewing and locking, as well as the ability to set scheduled or timed unlock permissions for family members or other visitors. At the same time, it can also integrate with Amazon Echo and other Ring doorbells and cameras you may already have at home.

The lock comes in three colours: black, silver, and brass, requires no additional wiring, and will be available early next year at US$249. To learn more, see here.

Brand New 4K Cameras

In addition to its first smart door lock, Ring has also launched several 4K cameras that support the new Retinal Vision 4K standard, meaning you'll enjoy excellent low-light footage and accurate colour reproduction. All of the following products are available for pre-order or purchase starting today:

  • Outdoor Cam 4K Plus: 140° wide field of view, with multiple power options including battery, plug-in, in-wall wired, and Power over Ethernet — US$149.99 on Amazon, see here for details
  • Floodlight Cam 4K Plus: powerful floodlights with 24/7 continuous recording and smart detection, requires in-wall wired connection — US$219.99 on Amazon, see here for details
  • Spotlight Cam 4K Plus: 550-lumen spotlight, 140° wide field of view, available in battery, plug-in, and solar configurations — US$199.99 on Amazon, see here for details
  • Indoor Cam 4K: Ring's first 4K indoor camera, supports dual-band Wi-Fi 6, 115° field of view — US$99.99 on Amazon, see here for details

Ring has also launched the new Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K at US$69.99, bringing 360° panoramic panning to a more affordable price point. It features motion tracking and a privacy shutter. To learn more, see here.
